text: Gold fell about 1.2% to near $3,983, back below $4,000, as the dollar surged and Fed hike bets rose after Tuesday's hot inflation report; it gave up its overnight bounce.
Silver ended roughly flat near $51.56 after fading from a morning bounce, so the gold/silver ratio dropped to about 77.3. SLV closed up 0.37% at $46.65.
The dollar index climbed about 0.7% to 102.92, its highest since April 2025, and USD/JPY rose to near 159.75, close to the 160 area where Japan has stepped in before.
The Nasdaq rose 1.6% and the S&P 500 1.3% as CoreWeave's jump revived AI stocks; QQQ closed up 2.31% at $690.38 and TQQQ about 7.3%. The VIX fell about 10% to 17.49.
After the close, Nvidia fell more than 8% in late trading on reports its board could consider removing the CEO, which could weigh on QQQ and TQQQ (and lift SQQQ) Thursday.
Brent rose about 1.5% to near $92.84 after Iran said tankers hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz; this matters for NRGU.
Treasuries did not trade Wednesday because of Veterans Day, so yields stay at Tuesday's levels (10-year 4.99%, 2-year 4.74%) until Thursday.
